title: whats the best engine to work with ai
author: Basic_Construction98
selftext:
I’ve been a software developer for years, but weirdly never became a game developer.

Games were actually the reason I got into programming in the first place.

But every time I tried making one, I quit.

Not because coding gameplay was hard.  
What killed it for me was the editors and all the tiny details around them.

Now with AI tools getting so good, I really want to try again.  
But I still feel way more comfortable with code-first engines than editor-heavy workflows.

What would you guys recommend?

comments.author: KevinDL
comments.body: Likely Unity right now due to the amount of options available.

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: Godot is plain text, which makes it very GenAI-friendly without MCP hooks. But in terms of available integrations, Unity and I think UE are catching up.

replies.author: Basic_Construction98
replies.body: my game will be 2d so i dont need complex integrations(but will need cool assets)

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: Definitely Godot then. The only engine I can think of that's more AI-Coding-Assistant friendly is RenPy for visual novels (given that it's basically a Python derivative) or stuff like LÖVE, which is also kind of cool (Balatro runs on that apparently) but not as well documented as Godot, which increases the errors GenAI will make. So yeah, Godot is probably your best bet.

replies.author: Useful_Use_6170
replies.body: Im currently using codex and it will generate assets for you and code it into godot or generate tour own assets upload to codex and tell it what u want it to do.

Claude Code is more than happy to launch the project, screenshot the scene then review its own work. Claude Design can also take your current game files as a base for a design system although I feel that using it to develop the layout then create a handover package for Claude Code is much better.

replies.author: Vlaxilla
replies.body: Claude code can Screenshot and show you? Claude design can make game assets?

Yeah, it just runs the cli command to open the scene -> takes a screenshot -> continues. You have to give it permission to but it’s just a single Allow prompt.

I don’t want to get you hopes up on the design side but simple hud layout design that the game engine can draw is no problem and honestly to the point 90% of my UI is drawn in engine instead of using a UI pack.

Another example is I’m running a day night cycle for my game, I used Claude design to build out the colours, timing the transitions and just had it create a mockup of how a 24hr cycle looked like. Once I was happy after maybe 5 revisions I asked it to create hand off documents and prompt to update in engine, adjusted the prompt manually and got 90% of the way there on the first prompt.

https://preview.redd.it/xvax49d5cwzg1.jpeg?width=1284&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=ec712a8c9e33cfa46b6c152bb966bdd4c885ead9

replies.author: siendo64
replies.body:
I recently worked with Claude Code to build a really nice pipeline for Godot to test in my Steam Deck.

I lay in bed prompting Claude code on the app. Then, I make a new PR. GitHub actions kick off headless Godot builds and smoke tests then post the binary as an artifact in a comment on the PR.

I then have a shell script I run on my steam deck that lets me select a Pr then it downloads the latest binary and runs it for testing.

comments.author: Panierowany
comments.body:
I use Godot (0 experience before) with Claude CLI, godotMCP, Gemini/Google Stitch for redesigns, and recently Claude Desktop (to utilize remote-control and the iOS Claude app so I can work while being in a taxi for example) + Codex for asset generation since the new image gen model and ElevenLabs MCP to generate SFX (although, to be honest, I got better results generating them directly on the site).

Godot has many plugins that give you things you need in game development like AdMob ads, Game Center support (iOS).   
I was even able to write my own plugin that gives me sliders in the Godot editor to tweak values like size, color, and element positions in real time.

At some point I also used GSD (Get Shit Done), which is basically a set of Claude skills. It helped a lot early on for discussing features in detail, although later in development it started slowing me down and consuming too many tokens. Still, I’d recommend it or a similar tool (or even just some simple skills that force you to discuss features with AI).

Overall, Godot + Claude works really well for my simple 2d mobile games development  

One thing though when I tried making some fancy lighting effects in one of my games, it made my phone hot and drained the battery pretty fast, even after multiple optimization attempts. I don’t know yet if it was my poor implementation, an actual Godot issue, or just a normal situation

comments.author: zoooobi_doooobi

Honestly, for someone with your background, I’d probably say:

* Godot if you want code-first + lightweight + AI-friendly
* Unity if you want maximum tutorials/assets/community
* Bevy if you’re a hardcore programmer who wants pure code workflows
* Unreal if you care about AAA visuals more than development speed
